page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor running at 3.2 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 8 vCPUs. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on a KVM hypervisor, lacks local storage, and has a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. There are no GPUs bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data reveals a mixture of average and weak performance characteristics. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng falls into the bottom 25%, and the Geekbench multi-core score is also in the bottom 25%. However, Geekbench single-core performance, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and text processing all register in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth read-only tests for both small and large blocks perform at average levels, whereas large block write bandwidth is weak.

In terms of workload fit, the instance demonstrates average capabilities for static web serving, Redis SET operations, and database operations. Large language model inference is limited, with average performance on a small 135M model but poor performance on a medium 7B model. Given the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the server offers a standard general-purpose profile, though its older Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 architecture results in lower computational efficiency compared to newer hardware classes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.2xlarge is a general-purpose server featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor at 3.2 GHz. It includes 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and operates on a KVM hypervisor with 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and no local storage. Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities for single-core tasks, software compilation, and database operations, though multi-core CPU performance and large block memory write bandwidth fall into the bottom 25%. LLM inference is limited, showing poor performance on medium 7B models. This server is suitable for standard general-purpose workloads, static web serving, and basic database operations where dedicated CPU allocation is required but extreme computational throughput is not.
